title: Marguerite and the Salt
premise: When the border wards of Thornfell collapse and the stars vanish, scribe Coral Hartwell discovers the wards were fed by salt mined by debt-bound laborers like himself—and that King Aldric has been hollowed out and worn as a vessel by the Salt King, an ancient hunger the temple once imprisoned. Guided by Marguerite, a disgraced ward-keeper who knows what the ritual truly costs, Coral must reach the capital before the coronation renewal seals the possession permanently. The price of unbinding is a life freely given to the salt, and in the end it is Coral—whose bloodline was the original seal—who pays it, freeing the king, restoring the stars, and winning Thornfell's debt-slaves their freedom at the cost of his own name being erased from every record he ever wrote.
about_author: Beatrix Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval salt-trade ledgers before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about ordinary people trapped in systems older and hungrier than they are.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Coral Hartwell, POV. In the mountain temple of Vael, Coral copies debt contracts for smugglers and laborers alike, secretly keeping his own forbidden ledger of everyone the temple owns. When the border wards shudder and the night sky goes starless, his mentor is found dead with salt crusted in her eyes. The emotional beat: quiet dread—the world Coral thought he understood has a hidden floor, and it just gave way.

chapters.title: What Wore the Crown
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV. Disgraced ward-keeper Marguerite Vane breaks into the royal archive and confirms her worst fear: the king's renewal rite failed because the wards were fed corrupted salt. She finds evidence that the original binding used Hartwell blood—a lineage officially extinct. The beat: cold, controlled terror as she realizes the only living Hartwell is a debt-scribe in the mountains.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Roads
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Temple inquisitors arrest Coral for his secret ledger, but Marguerite intercepts his transport on a smuggler's road only he knows. She tells him the truth: his blood can unbind the Salt King—or complete its freedom. He refuses and runs. The beat: furious denial; Coral would rather be nobody than be chosen.

chapters.title: The Starless Vale
chapters.summary: Coral, then Marguerite, POV. Alone in the darkened mountains, Coral sees what the fallen wards have unleashed: salt-eaten villages where people walk smiling and hollow. Marguerite catches up to him saving a child, and he grudgingly accepts her help—not the mission, just her. The beat: horror giving way to reluctant alliance; survival now requires trust.

chapters.title: Salt in the Blood
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV. Hiding in a free-town bathhouse, Marguerite teaches Coral the old ward-craft and tests his blood: it burns salt on contact. She confesses she helped design the failing wards years ago to buy her own pardon from the crown. The beat: guilt exchanged for guilt—two people complicit in different ways, deciding to stop running from it.

chapters.title: The Coronation Road
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. They infiltrate a pilgrimage caravan bound for the capital, passing through checkpoints where the possessed king's new edicts brand ward-keepers traitors. Coral witnesses a public execution of a child ward-touched girl and cannot look away this time. The beat: moral awakening—his ledger instinct turns outward; he starts recording the regime's crimes instead of hiding his own.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV. Inside the palace, they find King Aldric lucid for one stolen hour, begging them to end it even if it kills him. But the Salt King's high priestess reveals the trap: the unbinding rite requires a Hartwell to give themselves willingly, and the Salt King has been cultivating Coral's arrival all along. The beat: despair—the rescue was always an invitation.

chapters.title: Everything the Stars Owed
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Captured and offered a bargain—his freedom and his debts erased if he refuses the rite—Coral spends his last night copying one final ledger: every name the temple and crown ever owned, to be smuggled out by freed prisoners. Marguerite begs him to run. The beat: resolve born not of heroism but of bookkeeping—he will not let the powerful erase people, including himself.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Alternating Coral and Marguerite, POV. At the renewal ceremony, Coral gives his blood willingly while Marguerite holds the collapsing wards open against the priestess. The Salt King tears free of Aldric and offers Coral eternity; Coral answers with his ledger's names, anchoring his identity beyond the salt's hunger, and dissolves the entity along with himself. Aldric wakes weeping; the stars return. The beat: sacrificial climax—triumph purchased at total cost.

chapters.title: A Name in Every Hand
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV. Weeks later, the debt-bonds burn in the temple yard and Aldric, diminished but honest, signs emancipation. Marguerite distributes Coral's final ledger across Thornfell so that thousands now carry his name in their hands. In the last line, salt on a windowsill glimmers faintly warm—as if something kind survived. The beat: grief transmuted into belonging; memory as the truest form of power.
